requirement:
The requirements index links to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter
under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index`.
rationale:
The subject requires one thing: the requirements index must link to its documented-coverage-gaps subchapter. `requirements.test-coverage.index` is cited as context. It says the subchapter is generated whether the index is explicitly placed or automatically generated.

Three marked tests cover this obligation:

- **Explicitly placed index:** `src/index.rs#mod[tests]/fn[index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters]` builds a book with a `{requirements-index}` marker in a nested chapter at `appendix/requirements-index.md`. It asserts that the index content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that exactly one "Documented coverage gaps" sub-chapter exists, with path `appendix/requirements-index/coverage.md` and parent names `["Requirements index"]`. The link is therefore checked against the index's own location, and it points at a chapter that exists.
- **Automatically generated index:** `src/lib.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages]` has no marker, so the default index is generated. It asserts the same link, `[Documented coverage gaps](requirements-index/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that the coverage sub-chapter exists at `requirements-index/coverage.md`.
- **Index at a different path and number:** `src/execution_coverage/book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[generated_reports_inherit_the_requirements_index_hierarchy]` uses an index at `reports.md`, with and without a section number. It asserts that the parent content contains `[Documented coverage gaps](reports/coverage.html)`. It also asserts that the coverage chapter's path is `reports/coverage.md`, so the link matches the chapter.

Together these cover both cases the cited `index` requirement distinguishes, explicit and automatic placement. They also cover different index paths. A link that was missing, wrongly relative, or pointed at the wrong chapter would fail these assertions. I found no gap.
